findings.claim: Per ledger L7 an opt-out setting was the recorded answer, but the change adds no setting. The attribute is emitted unconditionally on netstandard2.1/net5+ targets, so users cannot disable it. The requirement makes the setting optional, but L7 records it as the decision.

receipt_plan.detail: Cite L7 ('Add an opt-out setting'). Check the generator options (MessagePackGeneratorOptions / AnalyzerConfigOptions) for any property that gates the attribute; none appears in the diff.

findings.claim: Users on NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK targets get no ExcludeFromCodeCoverage, so the acceptance criterion 'All generated code is decorated' is only partly met. The attribute exists on net462 and later (and netstandard2.0 has it in the BCL since 2.0). The #if guard appears to be overly conservative. The generator's own .NET Framework consumers keep the coverage skew.

receipt_plan.detail: Run snapshot tests for a netstandard2.0 or net472 compilation and confirm the attribute is compiled out. Then check whether ExcludeFromCodeCoverage exists in those references (it does in netstandard2.0 and net472).

findings.claim: The attribute and #if lines are placed after the XML doc comment and before the type. In the string-key and formatter templates, the nesting emitter may leave preprocessor directives indented or following a line without a newline. The output has directives at column 0 inside nested namespaces, which is valid, but it changes every generated snapshot that users may check in.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun generator snapshot tests and inspect the diff for the string-key formatter in nested-type and generic cases to confirm the #if directive starts on its own line and compiles.
